body.text: Meridian Logistics runs its analytics on an **Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool** fed by Azure Data Factory, with data landing in ADLS Gen2 from SAP S/4HANA, Manhattan WMS and the TMS shipment APIs. The platform was built by a previous vendor, documentation is limited and several stored procedures carry critical business logic.

Cloud4C proposes to migrate this estate to **Microsoft Fabric**, moving 84 pipelines, 36 notebooks, 210 tables and 140 stored procedures onto a Fabric Lakehouse and Warehouse. The approach re-platforms what can move as is and refactors procedures only where Fabric requires it, which keeps risk and effort under control.

The migration runs over twenty weeks and ends with a four week parallel run with daily reconciliation, so Synapse is decommissioned only after Meridian signs off on matching results. Purview will be rescanned against the new estate so lineage and the catalog stay current.

items: **Reduce platform cost**: Retire the always-on Synapse dedicated pool in favour of shared Fabric capacity.
**Migrate with no loss of logic**: Move every pipeline, table and stored procedure with documented mapping and test evidence.
**Prove data parity**: Run Synapse and Fabric in parallel with daily reconciliation before cutover.
**Keep reports running**: Repoint all 18 Power BI datasets to Fabric with no change for report users.
**Restore documentation**: Produce the inventory, mapping matrix and runbooks the current platform lacks.
**Maintain governance**: Rescan the new estate in Purview and rebuild end-to-end lineage.

body.text: Cloud4C experts help customers get the most out of their public cloud investment, the agility, flexibility and scalability the cloud offers, without it becoming your core business. Cloud4C consistently delivers high-quality results and end-to-end support to ensure cloud excellence, prevent downtime and ensure greater resilience. Our proposed solution for Meridian Logistics is informed by several key guiding principles:

rows: Transform and load data in accordance with defined requirements and data mappings; standardize metrics.
Processes that scale to ever-expanding data via a common extraction framework; data volumes gracefully handled.
Processes supportable by anyone with base-level skills.
Load and access data quickly, minimizing impact on other processes.
ETL & BI semantic layer easily changed to support evolving requirements.
Effective handling of data-quality, cloud-service and connection problems without significant impact.
Fast development of ETL & BI through structural simplicity and reuse of key components.

body.text: **Raw (Bronze) layer:** stores a one-to-one copy of source data in its original, unprocessed form with basic quality gates, a single repository for all data, supporting structured, semi-structured and unstructured formats. Validation is limited to basic quality & completeness checks.

**Integrated (Silver) layer:** the curated layer where data is cleaned, transformed and enriched for consistency, accuracy and completeness, used for exploration, preparation and data-quality analysis. More structured than Bronze; the data model is designed business-use-case-agnostic.

**Use-case (Gold) layer:** the trusted, ready-to-consume layer where models are prepared for business needs and decision-making. Highly structured, consistent, reliable, the single source of truth for the organization.
**Data delivery layer:** provides logic and processes user requests, APIs, web services, downstream systems, visualization, microservices.
**Job Orchestration:** managing and coordinating execution of data-processing jobs, scheduling, monitoring, dependency management, error/exception handling.

**Traceability & reconciliation:** data lineage and audit trails (where data came from, who accessed it, what processing steps, where stored) plus reconciliation comparing datasets to ensure consistency and accuracy.
**Constraint checks:** automated validation that data meets defined rules and relationships.
**Runtime Audits:** checks during processing to ensure jobs run efficiently and produce accurate results; surface bottlenecks and resource issues.
**Housekeeping:** archiving and purging to keep the lake clean, efficient, performant and cost-optimized.

In the target state, sources continue to land through Fabric Data Pipelines into OneLake. The Lakehouse holds the raw and curated zones while the Fabric Warehouse replaces the dedicated pool for the serving layer and Purview covers catalog and lineage.

**Silver and Gold**: notebooks and Warehouse T-SQL apply the migrated business logic
**Serving**: the Fabric Warehouse replaces the dedicated pool for reporting
**Consumption**: Power BI datasets are repointed to Fabric
**Governance**: Purview scans the new estate and rebuilds lineage
